title: Contextual circuit breakers with rollback-safe fallbacks and per-dimension thresholds
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement contextual circuit breakers that can be configured per-dependency, per-model-variant, and per-tenant. Breakers must use SLO-aware thresholds (latency p95, error-rate, error budget burn rate) and support rollback-safe fallback behaviors that preserve correctness and observable signals (non-silent failures). This ticket covers design, runtime hooks, metrics, and a minimal rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
technical_design: We will implement a multi-dimensional breaker registry indexed by scope: dependency (eg. redis.auth-cache), model-variant (gpt-small-quant), tenant-id. Each breaker evaluates three signals: rolling error-rate, latency p95 relative to SLO, and error-budget burn (5m and 1h windows). Thresholds are configurable per-scope with defaults: error-rate 3%, latency p95 > 1.5x SLO, or error-budget burn > 40% in 5m window. Tripping requires a two-step confirmation: soft-trip (probabilistic shedding at 20-80% based on severity) then hard-trip after sustained violation for cooldown window (default 90s). Breakers must support hysteresis and cooldown backoff with exponential increase to avoid flip-flop. Fallbacks are explicit policies attached to each breaker: model-fallback (downgrade to compatible smaller quantized model with output validation), region-fallback (route to warm standby region), degrade-features (disable streaming / function-calls), or fail-open-with-error (return standardized 503 with reason). All fallbacks are audit-logged and emit metrics. Rollbacks must be safe: if rollout of a fallback causes downstream SLO regressions, system must auto-revert to previous policy and mark as incident for investigation.
acceptance_criteria: Registry supports creating breakers with scope types: dependency, model-variant, tenant
Breakers evaluate rolling windows and emit metrics: breaker.state, breaker.trip_reason, breaker.prob_shed
Soft-trip probabilistic shedding reduces traffic and preserves real-time metrics for decisioning
Hard-trip triggers configured fallback and emits an audit event with fallback type and ticketable metadata
Hysteresis prevents >3 flips within 10 minutes for a single breaker scope
A small internal canary (10 tenants) can opt-in and exercise model-fallback without impacting global traffic
Documentation and runbook published with rollback steps and playbook for incidents
testing_plan: Unit tests for registry, evaluation logic, and cooldown/backoff math
Integration tests that simulate spiky latency and error injections to verify soft->hard trip transition
Chaos scenario in staging: kill model backend in us-west and assert region-fallback engages and SLA degrades within expected bounds
Load test with tenant isolation: confirm per-tenant breaker trips without global blips
Canary rollout: enable for 5% of traffic, monitor breaker metrics and error budget burn for 1h before full rollout
rollout_notes: Start with model-variant and dependency scopes in staging. Expose breaker config via Console feature flag under "configurations/reliability/circuit-breakers" for engineers. Canary to internal tenants first, collect metrics for 24h, then expand to 25% traffic. Pause rollout if error budget burn on canary > 25% over baseline or if rollback-safe fallback causes >5% increase in end-to-end latency.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design doc shared in Confluence (see links). Asked infra for an extra metric shard to host breaker state metrics.
2026-03-05: Spike completed to evaluate probabilistic shedding algorithm; chose a beta-Bernoulli sampler with decay for rate smoothing.
2026-03-09: Schema for breaker audit-events finalized after Security review; added tenant-id hashing to avoid PII exposure in logs.
2026-03-12: First PR opened for registry and evaluation loop (RFC + unit tests). Seeking review from @Maya and @Rajat.
2026-03-14: QA found edge case where model-fallback could return tokens incompatible with client validation; added pre-fallback validation gate and reject fallback if validation fails.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Fallback causes degraded user experience or data correctness. Mitigation: Add validation gate and conservative canary window; require SME sign-off for model-fallback policies.
Risk: Flip-flopping breakers thrash routing. Mitigation: Enforce hysteresis and exponential cooldown; central dashboard alerts on flip-rate.
Risk: Metrics cardinality explosion for per-tenant+model breakers. Mitigation: Default to tenant-sampled metrics (1%) and aggregate shards; allow high-cardinality only via opt-in.
Risk: Security/PII in audit logs. Mitigation: Hash tenant ids and redact request payloads in fallback audit events.
Risk: Incorrect fallback mapping (incompatible model). Mitigation: Maintain compatibility matrix and automated compatibility tests as part of CI.
notes: We intentionally keep soft-trip probabilistic shedding visible (not silent) so product teams can inspect degraded results. Design aligns with Redwood's thesis of predictable inference economics: controlled shedding buys latency headroom at cost of quality but avoids full outages. Follow-on work: UI controls for per-tenant SLA overrides and automated ML-validations for fallback outputs.
